name: AlaSQL
tagline: Pure-JavaScript in-memory SQL engine for browsers and Node.js that queries arrays, JSON, CSV and Excel files.
description: AlaSQL is a SQL database engine written entirely in JavaScript that runs in the browser, Node.js and other JS runtimes with no native dependencies. It executes most of SQL-99 (joins, grouping, subqueries, unions) over in-memory tables or plain arrays of objects, adds syntax for nested JSON and simple graph queries, and can read and write CSV, TSV, JSON and Excel (.xls/.xlsx) files, persist to localStorage or IndexedDB, and read SQLite files via SQL.js. It is best treated as a data-wrangling and reporting library inside an app rather than a durable database: transactions are limited and data lives in memory. The project is actively maintained under MIT, with v4.21.0 released in October 2026.
developer: Andrey Gershun, Mathias Rangel Wulff and contributors

scale.notes: Bounded by the JavaScript heap of the browser tab or Node process.

strengths: Runs SQL directly over JavaScript arrays and JSON with no server or native code
Reads and writes CSV, JSON and Excel (.xls/.xlsx) for import/export and reporting
Optional persistence to localStorage or IndexedDB in the browser
Wide SQL-99 coverage including joins, GROUP BY and subqueries
Mature, MIT-licensed and still actively released
weaknesses: Data lives in memory; not a durable store for large or critical data
Transactions are limited (only for the localStorage engine)
Interpreted JavaScript is much slower than WASM engines like DuckDB-Wasm or SQLite-Wasm on big datasets
Edge-case SQL semantics differ from mainstream databases
useCases: Client-side filtering, grouping and joining of JSON API results
Exporting app data to Excel or CSV from the browser
Quick data transforms in Node.js scripts
Prototyping SQL logic without a database server
notIdealFor: Analytics where DuckDB-Wasm or SQLite-Wasm are an option
